frameworkName: NIST SP 800-66 (HIPAA Security Rule Implementation Guide)
licenseNote: Public domain (U.S. Government publication). Summaries below are original, written for this application.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: Security management process
controls.summary: The vendor conducts a documented, periodic risk analysis covering systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for a risk analysis specific to ePHI systems, not a generic enterprise risk assessment that happens to mention healthcare data.

controls.title: Assigned security responsibility
controls.summary: A named security official is responsible for developing and implementing HIPAA security policies.
controls.validationGuidance: A named role/title is sufficient; matches the pattern of GLBA-1's qualified individual requirement.

controls.title: Workforce security and access authorization
controls.summary: Access to ePHI is granted based on role, with a documented authorization and termination process.
controls.validationGuidance: Check specifically for a documented offboarding/access-revocation step, a common gap area.

controls.title: Security awareness and training
controls.summary: Workforce members with ePHI access receive periodic security awareness training.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for training frequency and completion tracking, not just an acknowledgment of a training program's existence.

controls.title: Business associate agreements
controls.summary: A signed BAA is in place with any subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI on the vendor's behalf.
controls.validationGuidance: This is the HIPAA-specific analog to NIST 800-161's contractual flow-down control (C-SCRM-3) - check that BAA terms specifically reference ePHI, not generic confidentiality language.

controls.title: Facility access controls
controls.summary: Physical access to facilities and systems housing ePHI is controlled and monitored.
controls.validationGuidance: For cloud-hosted ePHI, this is typically satisfied by the underlying cloud provider's SOC 2/ISO certification - verify the vendor references it explicitly.

controls.title: Access control (technical)
controls.summary: Unique user identification, automatic logoff, and encryption/decryption controls govern access to ePHI.
controls.validationGuidance: Unique user IDs (no shared credentials) is a specific, checkable item distinct from general access-control assertions.

controls.title: Audit controls
controls.summary: Hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms record and examine activity in systems containing ePHI.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence logs are both generated and actually reviewed, not just retained.

controls.title: Transmission security
controls.summary: ePHI transmitted over electronic networks is protected against unauthorized access, using encryption where reasonable and appropriate.
controls.validationGuidance: Overlaps with GLBA-5; a single encryption-in-transit evidence excerpt commonly satisfies both frameworks.

controls.title: Contingency plan for ePHI systems
controls.summary: A tested data backup, disaster recovery, and emergency-mode operation plan exists for systems containing ePHI.
controls.validationGuidance: Should reference actual test/exercise results - overlaps with ISO 22301's continuity testing expectation.
